column1: # 21장 말투 지시. 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).

column2: A week later. Yuna has been avoiding Marc, a reserved locksmith, since she began to fear that Martí may be her real grandfather. On Sunday Marc waits at Montse's door with white flowers and, for the first time, asks something of her: to meet his grandfather at the cemetery. Yuna notes the grammar: "quiero que conozcas", not "quiero conocer"; after a wish for someone else, the verb changes form (conocer → conozcas). Quiet, uneasy.

column1: Quiero que conozcas a mi abuelo.
column2: serious and simple, a real request; stress "conozcas"
plain, then quietly sincere at "Te lo pido ahora"

Poblenou cemetery near the sea, a quiet city of marble niches. Marc explains that his grandfather Martí wanted to rest near the sea; Yuna knows why: the ship, the port, the island. At Martí's niche, Marc tells her Montse brings flowers every Sunday, then speaks to the stone in Catalan: "Avi, this is Yuna, Sun-rye's granddaughter. She came." Yuna understands it all. Hushed, tender.

column1: Mi abuela está en otro sitio.

column2: quiet, as if it were obvious
in Catalan, very softly, to the gravestone

At the grave, Yuna does the arithmetic: Martí was 26 in 1974, the year he was in Las Palmas. She thinks "Ojalá no sea verdad" (may it not be true) and understands the old word "ojalá" for the first time. Her question about other children sounds too loud in the silence; she brushes Marc off. Marc, unaware, wishes his grandfather is happy she is here. When he reaches for her hand, she steps back. Tense, painful, quiet.
too sudden, her voice strange in the silence
tender, to the gravestone and to her

On a bench at Bogatell beach, grey sea, sitting far apart. Marc says the pendulum is hung and asks her to be there to wind the clock with her key. Then he admits he is afraid she will never tell him what is wrong ("tengo miedo de que"). Yuna promises to tell him soon. Distant, quietly sad.

column1: Yuna, no sé qué te pasa.
